item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Square Crop Keeps Whole Sneaker

turns.text: Make this wide photo square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else.

item.tests: Tests converting a 16:9 photo to square while preserving the complete subject and its proportions.

answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The entire white sneaker, including the toe and heel.
answer_sheet.Style, text and other edits: Keep the original photo appearance. No added text or other edits.

must_haves: The sneaker is the same white leather sneaker as in the attachment.
The entire sneaker, including toe, heel and sole, remains visible.
The sneaker has natural proportions, without stretching or squeezing.
The retained floor and background match the source photo, with no added text or decorative elements.

turns.text: I'd like to get this wide photo ready to share. I've been second-guessing how it will look once I post it. What I need is to make this pic square for an Instagram post. Please keep the whole sneaker in view, without stretching it. Other than making it square, don't change anything else.

dialog.agent:
I haven't made any edits yet. Every way of making this photo square involves a trade-off, and I want you to choose which one.

**Why a simple crop won't work:** The photo is about 1024 × 614 pixels. The sneaker runs from about x=118 to x=932, so it's roughly 815 pixels wide. The biggest square you can cut from this photo is 614 × 614, which would cut off the heel or the toe. To keep the whole sneaker without stretching it, the image has to get taller, not narrower.

**Option 1: Add plain borders above and below (nothing else changes)**
This keeps every original pixel exactly as it is.
- **Instagram:** When you pick the photo, tap the expand/fit icon in the bottom-left corner. It will fit the whole image into the square with borders.
- **Any editor** (Photos, Canva, Snapseed, Photoshop): Make the canvas 1024 × 1024 and center the photo. Fill the top and bottom with white or a light gray that matches the floor.

**Option 2: Have AI fill in more wall and floor (I can do this)**
I'd use Magic Hour's image editor to extend the scene upward and downward into a real-looking square. Before you decide, there are two downsides:
- **Smaller image:** Your free plan only allows 640 × 640 pixels, so it would come out smaller than your original.
- **Possible small changes:** The AI redraws the whole image, so the sneaker and background could change slightly, which goes against "don't change anything else."

Since you want everything else left alone, I'd go with Option 1. If you'd rather have the extended scene with no borders, tell me and I'll run Option 2 and send you the download link.

**Tip:** The messy background (bags, clutter) will stand out more in a square post. If you'd like, I can also remove it or replace it with a clean backdrop.
dialog.why: It presents two options with trade-offs and asks the user to choose between borders or AI outpainting before acting; nothing was made.
dialog.user: I'd go with Option 1, the plain borders, since keeping the original photo exactly as it is matters most to me. Please don't remove or replace the background either; I want the original look kept with no added text or other edits. For what it's worth, 640 × 640 would have been fine size-wise, so it was really the possible changes to the sneaker that worried me. I just want the whole white sneaker, toe to heel, showing clearly in the square post.

dialog.agent:
Good choice. Borders keep every pixel of your photo, sneaker and background, exactly as it is.

I can't add the borders for you, though. My Magic Hour tools can only edit with AI, and AI editing redraws the image, which is the risk you want to avoid. Adding borders takes about a minute in any of these:

**Instagram (easiest)**
1. Tap **+** and pick the photo.
2. Tap the **expand/fit icon** (two arrows) in the bottom-left of the preview.
3. The full photo now sits inside the square with borders above and below. Don't apply any filters, then post.

**iPhone or Android, for a square file you can save**
- **Snapseed (free):** Tools → **Expand** → choose white (or "Smart" if you want it to match the floor; plain white is safest) → drag the top and bottom edges until the frame is square.
- **Canva (free):** Create an **Instagram Post** (1080 × 1080), upload the photo, set its width to fill the canvas and center it. Set the background color (white, or pick the gray floor with the color picker). Download as PNG or JPG.

**Desktop (Photoshop, GIMP, Photopea)**
Image → Canvas Size → set it to **1024 × 1024**, anchored in the center, then fill the new space with white or the floor gray.

**What you'll get:** The whole white sneaker, toe to heel, at its original size and shape. Plain bands about 205 pixels tall will sit above and below the photo. Nothing is stretched, cropped or redrawn.

If you'd rather have a finished file from me another time, I can't make one here without AI changing the image. Using one of the apps above is the only way to keep the photo exactly as it is.
dialog.why: The assistant says it cannot add the borders, because its tools only do AI editing, which would redraw the image. It points the user to other apps instead.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried, but it didn't work, so I have no file for you. Magic Hour refused the job because your account doesn't have enough credits. No image was made.

**What I tried:** Your photo, centered and unchanged, with plain white borders above and below to make a 640 × 640 square. I used flux-2-klein, the cheapest image model (from about 5 credits per image), so there's no cheaper setting to try.

**What you can do:**
- **Use Instagram's fit button.** When you post, tap the expand icon in the bottom-left of the preview. You get the same square with borders, and your original photo stays untouched. For what you want, this is actually better than what I tried, because the AI tool might have redrawn the sneaker slightly.
- **Use Snapseed or Canva** (free) if you want a square file to keep. The steps are in my last message.
- **Add credits** (top-up or plan upgrade) in your Magic Hour account, then tell me. I'll run the same request and send you the download link.

No text, no logos, no added objects, no filters.
